entries.name: soldier-walk-sheet.png
entries.prompt:
Paint a coherent EIGHT-FRAME WALK LOOP of this soldier. TWO different contact drawings are provided: Image 1 is contact A (the holster-side/near leg trails back); Image 2 is contact B (the holster-side/near leg crosses forward in front). Preserve BOTH leg configurations. Image 3 is a timing guide ONLY, not artwork. Both contact drawings fix the same identity, blue clothing, cap, olive pack, low rifle, elevated southeast/front-right camera and sharp gouache finish. You must not replace contact B with contact A again.

FOUR columns and TWO rows, transparent background, exactly eight complete sprites, large empty gutters. SAME body size, camera, light, head and upper-body detail across both rows. Frame 1 MUST reproduce Image 1's leg ownership, Frame 5 (first cell second row) MUST reproduce Image 2's opposite leg ownership. In the FIRST ROW the near/holster leg trails and then lifts, bends, passes forward. In SECOND ROW the near/holster leg starts crossing forward as in Image 2, then plants and moves backward as the far leg swings. The second row is NOT a duplicate of the first.
Phases: 1 contact A, 2 weight down/rear boot clearly lifted, 3 passing with one shoe airborne beside supporting shin, 4 airborne leg reaches forward ready for B; 5 contact B using Image 2 leg anatomy, 6 weight down/opposite rear shoe clearly lifted, 7 opposite passing one shoe airborne, 8 airborne leg reaches forward toward contact A. Alternating grounded shoes. Small natural body bob, steady two-handed rifle. No rigid leg sliding. Anatomical bent knees and ankles, full boots, arms remain stable rather than change grip each frame. In-place sequence, no movement across cell. Frame 8 leads into 1, no identical endpoint. Sharp painted facets, no blurred watercolor, no ground shadows, no labels, no guide colors, no scene/grid/borders. No mirrored upper bodies; the cap brim, rifle and backpack always face the same way.
entries.usage: First four frames only; generated second half repeated leg ownership and is not used.

entries.name: soldier-opposite.png
entries.prompt:
Edit this exact soldier into ONE new full-body walk CONTACT pose with OPPOSITE leg positions. Keep everything above the belt identical: face, cap, uniform, backpack, low-ready rifle, two gripping hands, elevated three-quarter front-right camera, upper-left lighting, style and proportions.

In the reference the leg below the screen-left belt pouch/holster trails BACK toward screen-left, while the other leg supports the body on the forward screen-right shoe. REVERSE THIS. The leg descending from the SCREEN-LEFT HIP UNDER THE BELT POUCH must now extend diagonally forward to SCREEN-RIGHT and DOWN, heel touching ground, ankle ahead of the body. Its thigh must visibly overlap IN FRONT OF the opposite thigh. The other leg, below the screen-right hip, extends back toward SCREEN-LEFT/UP with its heel lifted, toe behind the body. This is opposite leg ownership, NOT just both legs widened, NOT the same pose, NOT a mirrored character. Do not change facing or rifle or clothing to achieve it. Show the near thigh crossing in front and the far knee behind. Both soles follow the same imaginary ground plane. Anatomically plausible articulated hip/knee/ankle joints.
Crisp painted material planes, clear edges, sharp shading matching the master. Exactly one complete character with generous transparent margins and true alpha, no grid, text, shadow or extra figures.

In this reference the NEAR leg from screen-left hip crosses FORWARD and supports on screen-right, while the FAR leg's boot is lifted BACK at screen-left. The NEAR planted leg from the holster hip moves under the pelvis, nearly vertical supporting on ground. Keep its cargo pocket on the supporting thigh. Far raised foot is not planted; only ONE shoe on ground. This is leg crossing/airborne passing, not a wide contact or kneeling pose. Preserve anatomically intact trousers, boots, two hips/knees/ankles.

entries.name: walker-walk-sheet.png
entries.prompt:
Make eight hand-painted animation drawings of ONE grey zombie walking in place facing southeast/front-right. Image 1 is the approved character master; retain exactly its bald grey head, slack face, grey torn short-sleeve shirt, lighter grey ragged trousers, dark shoes and proportions. Image 2 is a chronological eight-pose walk guide ONLY. Image 3 is the sharp painted game's art style. No colored clothing. No limb textures stretched or warped.

A transparent production sheet with FOUR columns and TWO rows, exactly eight full figures with large empty gutters, read left-to-right then next row. Consistent size, elevated three-quarter orthographic camera and upper-left light, same visible front/right side in all frames. Head and pelvis positions coherent throughout, not eight independent portraits. Zombie shuffles slowly with a stooped back, loose bent elbows, subtle alternating arm swing, and real articulated knee/ankle bends.

IMPORTANT the two half-cycles use OPPOSITE legs. Frames 1-4: the NEAR leg (attached to the hip closest to viewer, screen-left hip) is FORWARD toward screen-right/down and supporting the body; the FAR leg trails toward screen-left/up, then lifts bent behind, passes through bent beside the support shin, then reaches forward. Frames 5-8: the NEAR leg is now BACK toward screen-left/up; the FAR leg is FORWARD and supporting, and the near leg lifts, passes, reaches. Exact eight phases: near heel contact; weight down/far foot lifted behind; far knee passing/one grounded shoe; far leg reaching/near heel rising; far heel contact; weight down/near foot lifted behind; near knee passing/one grounded shoe; near leg reaching toward initial contact. Clear ankle lift, not sliding planted feet. Do not repeat the first contact pose as the fifth. Preserve all original anatomy, no duplicated legs/hands. The guide colors must not appear. Make consecutive drawings flow as one loop with alternating foot ownership.

Crisp gouache planes and clean hard-edge silhouette, minimal brush texture, no blurry/soft airbrush. Full body each time, no foot/body truncation or contact shadows. Transparent alpha, no scene, labels, grid lines, borders, glow, text or extra characters.
